mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has fallen 6.2 points over three weeks to -24.3, and each further decline in transit use removes commuter footfall from high-street retail catchments, so RETAIL_REC keeps falling over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds its mean over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -20 percent change from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL rising to +16.4 together with GROCERY_PHARM rising to +10.6 is a household-stockpiling signature: discretionary spend is redirected to at-home consumption, so RETAIL_REC falls further over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above +10 while RESIDENTIAL rises above +15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days exceeds its last 14-day mean even while GROCERY_PHARM stays above +10 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +15.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES crossing below -20 marks an effective work-from-home directive; office-adjacent weekday retail demand disappears within days, so RETAIL_REC declines over the following week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses below -20 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES sits below -20, RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is not lower than over the preceding 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS recovering to -14.7 reflects spring weather pulling discretionary time outdoors; outdoor leisure substitutes for indoor shopping under capacity limits, so RETAIL_REC weakens over the next two weeks.
regime_hint: spring seasonal regime with indoor capacity limits
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days rises toward baseline while PARKS continues improving toward baseline over the same window.

mechanism_narrative: The joint collapse of TRANSIT to -24.3 and WORKPLACES to -20.6 is a synchronised withdrawal of commuting trips; the two series reinforce each other, so RETAIL_REC falls more than either series alone implies over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -20 and WORKPLACES below -15 at the same time
failure_condition: When TRANSIT is below -20 and WORKPLACES below -15 simultaneously, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not lower than its last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under an explicit stay-at-home regime, RESIDENTIAL above +15 is a direct measure of at-home containment that suppresses out-of-home retail trips, holding RETAIL_REC below its current level for four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds +15 percent change from baseline
regime_hint: tightening restrictions with an active stay-at-home instruction
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds its last 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL remains above +15 throughout.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossing +10 marks the peak of precautionary stockpiling; as pantry inventories deplete precautionary demand unwinds and spending reverts toward general retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above +10 percent change from baseline
regime_hint: late tightening, before any announced easing
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days stays at or below its last 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +10 for the whole window.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing below -20 while WORKPLACES drops more than 5 points week-on-week signals retail capacity rules about to tighten; operators pre-empt the announcement, so RETAIL_REC drops within the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses below -20 and WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
regime_hint: tightening restrictions announced but not yet fully in force
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the week after this joint crossing is equal to or higher than in the week before it.
